stories.headline: Update: Trump Confirms He Secretly Switched Planes at NATO Summit to Evade Iranian Threat
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday publicly confirmed that he was moved off Air Force One following last month's NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, due to a credible Iranian assassination threat. Trump was hidden inside an airport catering container and transferred to a separate military aircraft while Air Force One was sent aloft as a decoy. The extraordinary security operation was first reported by The Washington Post on Monday.

Trump sought to downplay the unusual nature of the maneuver, telling reporters the Secret Service and military advised him to board a different plane and that he complied. 'I get a lot of threats,' he said, adding he did not ask many questions about the specifics of the danger. He also minimized the risk to White House staff, security personnel, and journalists who remained on Air Force One during the decoy flight.

The confirmation marks a materially new development in the story, as Trump himself is now on record acknowledging the incident for the first time. The episode raises questions about the security protocols surrounding presidential travel and the extent of Iranian threat activity targeting U.S. officials during the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict that began in February.

Thirteen news outlets are covering Trump's confirmation, making it one of the most widely reported stories of the day. The incident underscores both the elevated threat environment facing the administration and the lengths to which the Secret Service is going to protect the president.

stories.headline: DOJ Charges Former SPLC Official Heidi Beirich in Superseding Indictment Against Civil Rights Group
stories.summary:
The Department of Justice on Wednesday charged Heidi Beirich, a former senior official at the Southern Poverty Law Center, in a superseding indictment related to the government's broader criminal case against the Alabama-based nonprofit. Beirich, who previously served as the SPLC's chief financial officer and was widely known as a leading expert on far-right extremism, faces charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and related financial crimes. Prosecutors allege she oversaw payments totaling $4.1 million in donor funds to informants embedded in hate groups, including payments for items such as KKK robes and cross burnings.

The charges are the first brought against an individual in the SPLC case. The DOJ alleges the funds were misrepresented to donors and used in ways that constitute fraud. Beirich's attorney pushed back sharply, stating: 'A free and fair society does not use the justice system to silence its political opponents.'

The SPLC has long been a target of conservative critics who contend the organization is politically biased and misuses its 'hate group' designations against mainstream conservative organizations. Supporters of the SPLC argue the prosecution is an example of the Trump administration weaponizing federal law enforcement against civil society groups that have historically monitored the far right.

Eight outlets are covering the story, which carries significant implications for free speech, nonprofit accountability, and the Justice Department's approach to civil rights organizations under the current administration.

stories.headline: Moderate David Crowley Wins Wisconsin Democratic Gubernatorial Primary, Sets Up Fall Race Against Trump-Backed Tom Tiffany
stories.summary:
Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley won Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary on Tuesday, defeating democratic socialist state Rep. Francesca Hong in a razor-thin contest that was not decided until early Wednesday morning. Crowley, who would become Wisconsin's first Black governor if elected, pitched himself as a cross-aisle coalition builder best positioned to win the November general election in the key swing state.

Crowley will face Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, who has voted with President Trump 100 percent of the time, in the November midterm contest. Former Republican Gov. Scott Walker acknowledged Tiffany will need to carefully manage questions about his Trump alignment, saying the congressman must tell voters 'that's not what's on the ballot.' Crowley, for his part, pledged to unite his party's progressive and moderate wings, framing the race as Democrats versus 'a MAGA extremist.'

The primary result reflects broader tensions inside the Democratic Party between its establishment and insurgent progressive wings. Crowley's margin over Hong was less than one percentage point, meaning neither ideological faction can claim a decisive mandate. The outcome mirrors a similarly close Michigan Senate Democratic primary the previous week, where a progressive candidate narrowly defeated a moderate backed by the governor.

With twelve outlets covering the story and Wisconsin having been decided by narrow margins in recent presidential cycles, the governor's race is seen as a bellwether for 2028 White House prospects and a test of which Democratic approach can win back Midwestern swing voters.

stories.headline: Update: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Reaches 265 as Survivor Pulled Alive After 36 Hours
stories.summary:
The death toll from Colombia's 7.4-magnitude earthquake has risen to at least 265, with 496 people still reported missing, President Abelardo de la Espriella announced Wednesday. The quake, which struck Monday near the village of San José del Palmar in Chocó province, has caused widespread destruction across western Colombia, with the cities of Cali and Pereira sustaining the highest casualties.

In a dramatic rescue Wednesday, a 32-year-old woman named Daniela Largo was pulled alive from the rubble in Pereira after a 10-hour operation, having been trapped under four concrete slabs for 36 hours. Firefighters dug two tunnels to reach her — one from above to provide oxygen and one from below to extract her. President de la Espriella hailed her rescue as 'news which fills us with hope.' Largo's 12-year-old son had been awaiting her rescue at home.

More than 200 people remained trapped in Cali as of Tuesday afternoon, with at least 92 buildings collapsed in Pereira alone. Cali's mayor declared a nighttime curfew and deployed soldiers in the worst-hit areas to ensure rescue operations could proceed safely. More than 100 aftershocks have been recorded since the initial quake.

This update brings a material increase in the confirmed death toll — up from more than 200 in previous coverage — and adds the significant new development of a confirmed survivor rescue deep into the emergency response window.
